title: League of Legends Patch 26.15 Notes
overview: Patch 26.15 headlines a brand-new retro game mode, League of Legends Classic, alongside a heavy Bel'Veth early-game gutting and nerfs to snowballing solo-lane carries like Riven, Sylas, Naafiri and Mordekaiser. Ranked also gets structural changes: Aegis of Valor stops shielding LP losses, and apex duo queue is restricted.
summary: Bel'Veth got gutted early: 0.85 → 0.67 base attack speed, 60 → 55 AD, 610 → 580 HP, and Q is now on a real cooldown at rank 1.
Snowball carries reined in — Riven's R ratio, Sylas Q first lash, Naafiri's ult, and Mordekaiser's R stat steal all shrank.
Alistar, Kai'Sa, Maokai, Volibear and Zac all got buffs, so tanky engage and scaling ADC picks look better.
Yun Tal Wildarrows is 100g cheaper with more attack speed, and Bastionbreaker got cheaper with a bigger Shaped Charge hit.
changelogHighlights: League of Legends Classic — a new retro game mode with 60 champions using their classic early-League kits.
Arena augment shakeup: Slow and Steady removed, Ok Boomerang's level 2 now fires a second boomerang, and several augments capped at level 2.
Bruisers and snowball carries were nerfed while tanks and scaling picks got buffed.

champions.summary: Sweeping early-game nerfs across stats and every ability.
champions.details: Base attack speed drops 0.85 → 0.67, attack damage 60 → 55, and health 610 → 580, while Q's cooldown goes from a flat 1 second to 4/3.25/2.5/1.75/1, W's slow falls 50% → 30%, E's cooldown rises 20-16 → 24-12, and R's buff duration now scales with stacks instead of a flat 60/180 — so early jungle clear, skirmishing, and dueling are all noticeably weaker and you need to play for scaling.
champions.name: Bel'Veth

champions.summary: Lower health, weaker Q, capped W move speed, and less Grey Health.
champions.details: Health drops 655 → 620, Q damage is reduced, W's move speed is now capped at 40%, and Grey Health scaling is reduced, meaning less bully potential in lane and less forgiveness when you take a bad trade.
champions.name: Locke

champions.summary: R steals fewer stats, though E comes back faster.
champions.details: Realm of Death's stolen stats fall 13% → 10% while E's cooldown improves 18-10 → 16-8, so your 1v1 ult swing is smaller even though you can pull people in more often — winning a Death Realm no longer snowballs the rest of the fight as hard.
champions.name: Mordekaiser

champions.summary: Ultimate damage cut at every rank.
champions.details: R damage drops 150/225/300 → 125/200/275 with reduced per-packmate damage, so all-in assassinations that used to just barely kill will now leave targets alive.
champions.name: Naafiri

champions.summary: Ultimate bonus AD ratio and Wind Slash damage reduced.
champions.details: R's bonus AD ratio falls 25% → 20% and Wind Slash goes 60-180% → 55-165%, so your execute range shrinks and low-health enemies escape combos that used to finish them.
champions.name: Riven

champions.details: Chain Lash's first lash drops 40-140 → 40-120 at max rank, weakening his poke and wave-clear pattern in lane.
champions.name: Sylas

champions.details: Move speed goes 330 → 335, making it a little easier to land Headbutt-Pulverize engages and roam between lanes.
champions.name: Alistar

champions.summary: Passive Caustic Wounds scales harder at max level.
champions.details: Caustic Wounds scaling increases 4-24 → 4-30 at max level, so her plasma detonations hit harder into the late game and she's a stronger scaling carry.
champions.name: Kai'Sa

champions.summary: Q hits monsters harder and gets a bigger AP ratio.
champions.details: Q monster damage goes 140-180% → 150-190% and its AP ratio 40% → 50%, improving both jungle clear speed and AP Maokai's damage output.
champions.name: Maokai

champions.summary: Q cooldown lowered at early ranks.
champions.details: Q's cooldown improves 14-10 → 12-10 seconds, giving him more frequent stuns for early skirmishes and ganks.
champions.name: Volibear

champions.summary: More armor growth and a faster E.
champions.details: Armor growth rises 4.7 → 5.2 and E's cooldown drops 22-10 → 21-9 seconds, so he's tankier as the game goes on and can throw himself into fights more often.
champions.name: Zac

items.summary: Cheaper and grants more attack speed.
items.details: Cost drops 850g → 750g and attack speed rises 40% → 45%, making it a faster and stronger crit spike for ADCs.
items.name: Yun Tal Wildarrows

items.summary: Cheaper with a stronger Shaped Charge.
items.details: Cost falls 3200g → 3000g and Shaped Charge's base damage goes 30 (+150% lethality) → 50 (+150% lethality), so lethality bruisers and assassins get to their power spike sooner and hit harder when they do.
items.name: Bastionbreaker

items.summary: Shadow effect now scales with AD and AP.
items.details: The Shadow effect's flat 30 magic damage becomes 30 (+10% bonus AD) (+10% AP), so the item stays relevant later into the game as you build damage.
items.name: Terminus

systems.summary: League of Legends Classic, a retro game mode, is released.
systems.details: League Classic features 60 champions using classic versions of their gameplay from early League history and leans on strategy over mechanics, giving players a completely different queue to play.

systems.summary: Aegis of Valor no longer softens losses but doubles LP on wins.
systems.details: Aegis of Valor will no longer reduce LP losses on defeat, and wins award double LP without requiring a minimum mastery score — so bad games hurt full price now and there's no reason to hold it for a safety net.

systems.summary: Duo queue restricted at the top of the ladder.
systems.details: Master players may now duo but only with players close to them in rank, while GM, Challenger, and anyone with GM or Challenger MMR cannot duo at all, so high-elo players will be soloing more often.

systems.summary: Jack of All Trades gives less Adaptive Force per breakpoint.
systems.details: Adaptive Force at its breakpoints drops 10/25 → 8/20, making the rune a weaker payoff for stacking varied legendary stats.

systems.summary: Crit-to-Adaptive conversion improved and several augments capped at level 2.
systems.details: Critical strike now converts to Adaptive Force at 1:1 instead of 0.68:1, Slow and Steady is removed, Ok Boomerang's level 2 fires a second boomerang, and several augments can no longer be upgraded past level 2 — so crit-heavy champions gain and the strongest augment scaling paths are cut off.

systems.summary: Damage modifiers now apply to every damage source, plus 30+ champion tweaks.
systems.details: Damage dealt modifiers now apply to spell, attack, item, and Augment damage, Critical Missile damage is reduced, and over 30 champions were rebalanced — meaning the champion you're used to abusing in Mayhem may feel very different.
